subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How long before the Paper 3 examination does AQA issue the pre-release resources booklet?
questions.explain: AQA releases the pre-release resources booklet 12 weeks before the Paper 3 exam so students can become familiar with the issue.

questions.q: Which AQA GCSE Geography paper contains the issue evaluation?
questions.explain: The issue evaluation is Section A of Paper 3, Geographical applications.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the pre-release resources booklet?
options: To be memorised and copied word-for-word in the exam
To let students study a geographical issue and its resources before the exam
To replace the need for fieldwork
To give students the exam mark scheme in advance
questions.explain: The booklet allows students to explore a contemporary geographical issue and its resources ahead of the exam.

questions.q: What proportion of the total GCSE marks does Paper 3 (Geographical applications) carry?
questions.explain: Paper 3, Geographical applications, is worth 30% of the AQA GCSE Geography qualification.

questions.q: The highest-mark questions in the issue evaluation typically require students to:
options: describe a single resource in detail
evaluate options and reach a justified decision
draw an accurate map from memory
questions.explain: Top-level issue evaluation answers weigh up different options and justify a chosen decision using the resources.

questions.q: A student must decide which of three flood-management options is best for a river valley. Which approach would gain the most marks?
options: Choose the cheapest option without giving reasons
State a personal opinion with no supporting evidence
Use evidence from the resources to justify a choice while acknowledging drawbacks
List all three options without reaching a decision
questions.explain: Justified decisions supported by evidence from the resources, recognising limitations, score highest.

questions.q: How many fieldwork enquiries must AQA GCSE Geography students carry out?
questions.explain: Students must undertake two geographical enquiries as part of the course.

questions.q: The two required fieldwork enquiries must be based on:
options: one physical and one human geography topic
one classroom and one online topic
questions.explain: AQA requires one physical and one human geography enquiry in contrasting environments.

questions.q: What is normally the first stage of the geographical enquiry process?
options: Creating a suitable enquiry question or hypothesis
questions.explain: An enquiry begins by identifying a suitable question or hypothesis to investigate.

questions.q: Why do students complete a risk assessment before fieldwork?
options: To increase the amount of data collected
To identify hazards and reduce dangers in the field
To choose which graphs to draw
To calculate the mean of their results
questions.explain: A risk assessment identifies potential hazards and ways to reduce risk during fieldwork.

questions.q: Primary data is best described as data that is:
options: collected first-hand by the student in the field
questions.explain: Primary data is collected first-hand by the investigator during fieldwork.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of secondary data?
options: Measurements you take of river width
A questionnaire you hand out yourself
Census population data published by the government
questions.explain: Secondary data, such as census statistics, is collected and published by someone else.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of qualitative data?
options: The number of pedestrians counted per minute
River velocity in metres per second
People's written opinions about a new development
The height of a beach in metres
questions.explain: Qualitative data describes qualities or opinions rather than numerical measurements.

questions.q: In systematic sampling, data is collected:
options: at regular intervals, such as every 10 metres
only where the results look interesting
by dividing the population into groups
questions.explain: Systematic sampling takes measurements at fixed, regular intervals.

questions.q: A student wants each shopping street in a town to be represented in proportion to its size within a survey. Which sampling method is most appropriate?
questions.explain: Stratified sampling divides the population into groups so each is represented in proportion to its size.

questions.q: A choropleth map shows data by:
options: shading areas in different colours or densities according to value
drawing lines that join points of equal value
using arrows of different widths to show movement
questions.explain: Choropleth maps use graded shading to show how a variable varies between areas.

questions.q: A student wants to see whether river depth increases with distance downstream. Which is the most suitable graph?
questions.explain: A scatter graph shows the relationship between two variables and reveals any correlation.

questions.q: The median of a data set is:
options: the middle value when the data is placed in order
the difference between the highest and lowest values
the sum of the values divided by how many there are
questions.explain: The median is the middle value of a data set arranged in numerical order.

questions.q: When analysing results, a student finds one point that lies far outside the general trend. This point is best described as:
questions.explain: A value that does not fit the general pattern of the data is called an anomaly.

questions.q: In the evaluation stage of an enquiry, a student should mainly:
options: assess the reliability of the methods and suggest improvements
questions.explain: Evaluation involves judging the reliability and limitations of the enquiry and suggesting how it could be improved.

specSource: AQA GCSE Geography (8035) specification; Geographical Applications (Issue Evaluation & Fieldwork)
